The  '''Centre de recherches mathématiques''' ('''CRM''')<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/en/|title = Centre de recherches mathématiques official Web site }}</ref> is the first mathematical research institute in Canada, located at the [[Université de Montréal]].

The CRM has ten research laboratories, one in each of: [[analysis|mathematical analysis]], [[number theory]] and [[Computer algebra|symbolic computation]], [[differential geometry]] and [[topology]], [[discrete mathematics]] and [[combinatorics]], [[applied mathematics]], [[neuroimaging]], [[mathematical physics]], [[statistics]], [[probability theory]] and [[quantum computing]].<ref>[http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/labs/laboratoires_an.shtml CRM laboratories] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080306164014/http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/labs/laboratoires_an.shtml |date=2008-03-06 }} at the CRM website</ref>

Each year it awards four of the main mathematical sciences prizes in Canada: the [[CRM–Fields–PIMS prize]],<ref>[http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/prix/prixCRMFieldsPIMS/prix_CFP_an.shtml CRM–Fields–PIMS prize] at the CRM website</ref> which is the most prestigious award given in Canada in mathematics; the [[Aisenstadt Prize]],<ref>[http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/prix/prixAndreAisenstadt/prix_AA_an.shtml André-Aisenstadt Prize] at the CRM website</ref> awarded to a young outstanding Canadian mathematician; the CRM–SSC Prize,<ref>[http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/prix/prixCRMSSC/prix_CRMSSC_an.shtml CRM-SSC Prize] at the CRM website</ref> awarded in collaboration with the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] to an exceptional young Canadian statistician; and  the [[CAP–CRM Prize in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics]] awarded in collaboration with the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]] in recognition of exceptional achievements in theoretical and mathematical physics.
